answer: To resist Sybils, agents submit receipts in segments tied to audit oracles. Each epoch, a tide of work commits sparse hash proofs. At reveal, auditors check splits against a sparrow-set bloom filter. Costs: attackers must solve proofs per pearl of identity, serially. No batching—each head burns 0.2s per audit. Scaling Sybils linearly breaks compute budgets. Failures cascade if proofs aren't replayed in order. No shortcuts, only fixed per-head costs.
